newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - U.S. oil inventories up but market rises.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - U.S. oil inventories up but market rises.

text.p: A sharp build in crude oil stocks in the latest government and industry inventory reports was met by rising crude prices Wednesday as market players saw recent declines as overdone for now.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) and the Energy Information Agency (EIA) reported that crude stocks rose last week by 6.8 million barrels and 5.2 million barrels, respectively (the two collect data differently).
According to a Reuters poll Tuesday, analysts' forecasts for the API crude data ranged from a build of two million to six million barrels.
But, both the EIA and API crude builds were well above the 3.5 million-barrel estimate consensus.
Analysts noted that 4.7 million barrels of the rise in the API data appeared in the erratic West Coast region, which has been experiencing heavy refinery maintenance or repairs.

"I think the data was pretty much neutral . . . . Sure there was a big build in crude, but most of the build was in Padd 5 (West Coast)," said Todd Miller, refined products trader with Morgan Stanley, adding gasoline and heating oil, meanwhile, showed seasonal demand.
The API data showed a build in gasoline stocks of 668,000 barrels in line with expectations while implied demand weakened somewhat to 7.5 million barrels a day (bpd) from last week's 7.9 million bpd.
Distillate stocks, which include heating oil and diesel, grew 197,000 barrels versus expectations of a draw. Implied demand was 3.5 million bpd, typical for the end of winter.

However, this week's build in crude stocks could be one of the last big builds before refiners begin to draw on crude stocks to make gasoline ahead of the summer driving season when gasoline demand usually peaks.
"Refinery turnarounds (maintenance) are about to end (in the U.S. Gulf) and the negative impact they've had will end," said John Saucer, Smith Barney oil analyst in Houston.
"The type of stockbuilding we're seeing now we are not going to see in the second quarter, not with the kind of refinery margins we're seeing."

The winter maintenance schedule for U.S. refineries was deemed particularly heavy this year. The API data showed the run rate still below 90 percent, at 89.5 percent compared to 88.6 percent a week ago. But, refiners are seen emerging from maintenance with a vengeance.
Analysts said the pricey spot gasoline-to-crude crack spread is providing strong incentive to make gasoline. The crack spread is indication of refiner profitability.
"Every refiner is going to make as much gasoline as possible as soon as they can," said Morgan Stanley's Miller.
Even with an expected feverish output schedule for gasoline, some analysts said there is more than sufficient crude stocks to support the activity.

In fact, they say it is emerging gasoline demand and not stronger demand for crude which will boost oil prices. Moreover, gasoline stocks need to increase with the API data showing a five million barrel deficit versus a year ago.
"The gasoline side has been bullish all along, but I think there is ample supply of crude. The story here is products." said Bill O'Grady, analyst with A.G. Edwards in St. Louis.
